_comment: run_to_run is MEASURED, not asserted. tests/spine/derive-run-to-run.sh applies
one catalog to an identical starting state twice with Ruby, deep-diffs the two
to_data_hash reports, and fails if this list is either incomplete (a leaf differs
that no pattern covers) or over-broad (a pattern also suppresses a leaf that did
NOT differ). Re-run it rather than editing this list by hand: an allowlist you
cannot re-derive is a claim, and every field in it is a field the differential
will never report.
Last derived: 21 differing leaves, every one a timestamp or a UUID, covered by the
18 patterns below. The pattern count exceeds the number of distinct field SHAPES
because the metrics.time entries are named individually rather than wildcarded --
see the note below on why.
metrics.time.values.package.value and metrics.time.values.exec.value are the two
entries derive-run-to-run.sh cannot validate: it reports them UNUSED, because the
HOST fixture has neither a package nor an exec resource and cannot have either --
Puppet on the host resolves the dnfmodule provider, so a package would measure the
wrong subsystem, and the host Ruby cannot fork under Puppet, so an exec dies with
Errno::EBADF before running. Their provenance is the CONTAINER fixture instead:
report-diff-container.sh's catalog applied twice with Ruby in two fresh containers
measured 7.21s against 14.98s for the package leaf, and 0.022280766 against
0.030870218999999997 for the exec leaf (measured 2026-09-26, with
`gatekit run-to-run` naming it the only uncovered differing leaf that
is not a failure detail). UNUSED is tolerated by the gate and OVER-BROAD is not,
so these two entries are checked by the measurements recorded here rather than by
dev:derive-run-to-run. If the host fixture ever gains a package or an exec, they
become derivable and the note can go.
metrics.time.values.service.value is UNUSED on the host for the same kind of
reason: Puppet selects the systemd provider only when systemd is PID 1, which the
host is not. Its provenance is report-diff-systemd.sh's catalog applied twice with
Ruby in two fresh systemd-booted containers: 1.044489995 against 1.144156349
(measured 2026-10-05, `gatekit run-to-run` naming it the only uncovered differing
leaf that is not journal text inside a failure message).
metrics.time.values.anchor.value, file_line.value, vox_prefetch.value,
vox_value.value, concat_file.value, concat_fragment.value, vox_evalgen.value,
vox_gen.value and tidy.value are UNUSED on the native host fixture too: those are the Tier 3
types report-diff-extension.sh's fixture applies through the extension host. Their
provenance is that fixture's catalog applied twice with Ruby from an identical
starting state, `gatekit run-to-run` reporting each one '1 differing, 0 stable'
(measured 2026-10-07). The last four were measured when the fixture gained
concat and generation: two Ruby-vs-Ruby pairs, each naming all four as
differing leaves no pattern covered -- concat_file 0.000124962 against
against 7.0131e-05 and 9.9781e-05 against 9.2371e-05, vox_evalgen 6.638e-05
against 6.7072e-05 and 8.926e-05 against 8.5831e-05, vox_gen 3.376e-05 against
4.6831e-05 and 4.669e-05 against 4.317e-05. tidy.value was measured the same
way when the fixture gained a walk-order case (2026-10-08): two Ruby-vs-Ruby
pairs, each naming it the only differing leaf no pattern covered -- 3.059e-05
against 4.035e-05 and 4.553e-05 against 3.494e-05.
metrics.time.values.augeas.value through user.value, the last eighteen, are the
SIMP catalog's resource types,
UNUSED on every other fixture. Their provenance is `DERIVE=1 bash
tests/spine/report-diff-simp.sh`, that catalog applied twice with Ruby in two fresh
systemd-booted containers (measured 2026-10-08), `gatekit run-to-run` naming
each one a differing leaf no pattern covered -- augeas 0.437833018 against
against 0.032564789, init_ulimit 0.210366198 against 0.192941253,
kernel_parameter 0.079737514 against 0.054386089, mount 0.018128603 against
against 0.296317461, selinux_state 0.004058085 against 0.004100436,
simp_file_line 0.00094088 against 0.000928691, ssh_config 1.33583391 against
1.423825672, sshd_config 1.265883259 against 1.252507982, sshd_config_subsystem
run names tidy.value, already listed, as differing. With these entries the
derivation leaves no differing leaf uncovered, but it still exits 1: it reports
resource_statuses.*.evaluation_time OVER-BROAD, with 8 stable leaves, each the
null evaluation_time of a resource both runs skipped. That pattern is shared
with every other gate and is left as it is; docs/maintainers/apply-spine.md,
'The SIMP gate', records why.
metrics.time.values.sshkey.value, the fourth-from-last entry, is UNUSED on every fixture but
G5's sshkey half (tests/spine/sshkey/g5.sh). Its provenance is that half's

fresh localhost/fleet-node-el containers (measured 2026-11-26), `gatekit

but G5's inifile half. Its provenance is that half's cases/section-create catalog
applied twice with Ruby (`puppet apply --catalog --libdir`, puppetlabs-inifile 6.6.1
with PR #581's lib hunk in the libdir) in two fresh localhost/fleet-node-el

The metrics.time entries are named, not indexed, because the comparator
re-keys each metric group from Puppet's positional [name, label, value]
triples before flattening. Indexed, the only usable pattern was
'metrics.time.values.*.2' -- and fnmatch's * crosses dots, so anything
broader also suppressed the metric NAMES and LABELS.
config_retrieval is deliberately ABSENT from this list. Measured: it is not
a duration that rounds to zero, it is a structural zero -- `puppet apply
--catalog` is handed its catalog and never retrieves one. voxagent does not
retrieve one either, so the two must agree on 0, and allowlisting it would
discard a real assertion. This gate fails if it is added back.
cross_implementation keys are read as path patterns by the comparator,
with two deliberate exceptions, because logs are compared as a multiset
rather than by path and no pattern can reach a log ENTRY. 'logs (Puppet:
Wrapped exception)' is shaped so it cannot be mistaken for a path, and it
matches nothing; the drop it declares lives in drop_wrapped_exception_logs.
A key 'logs (source: <source>)' drops, from both sides, every log entry whose
source is exactly <source> -- string equality, not a pattern. A path pattern
naming a resource writes its '[' as '[[]', because fnmatch reads a bare one as
the start of a character class.
Neither that entry nor failure_detail belongs in run_to_run -- one is a log
Ruby emits on every run, the other a substring rather than a whole leaf, and
derive-run-to-run.sh would call both OVER-BROAD.

cross_implementation.puppet_version: Ruby reports its own version; Go cannot match it and must not pretend to
cross_implementation.logs (Puppet: Wrapped exception): read from resource_harness.rb:149, Ruby logs the ResourceError itself, so util/logging.rb's format_exception appends a 'Wrapped exception:' line and the original Errno's message beneath the wrapper -- an embedded newline in a log message. voxagent reproduces the OTHER Puppet-sourced log, property.rb:496's bare wrapper, but not the chain: Ruby exception-chain rendering has no Go analogue worth inventing. Dropped from the RUBY side only, so the same log appearing on the voxagent side would still surface as a divergence

normalisation.logs: compared as a multiset -- voxagent commits to its own deterministic walk order rather than reproducing Puppet's, so log ORDER is not a divergence but log CONTENT is
normalisation.applied_catalog_duration: the 'Applied catalog in N.NN seconds' notice embeds a duration, which is run-to-run variance of the same class as a timestamp but sits inside a message rather than a field of its own, so no path-shaped allowlist entry can reach it -- the number is masked and the rest of the line is still compared
normalisation.failure_detail: a failure message embeds the underlying error's own text, and Ruby's is the name of the temp lockfile its file provider writes -- measured 2026-09-19 as 'bad.txt20260919-485055-vpdn4b.lock', carrying a date, a time and a random token -- so it varies between two RUBY runs and is not comparable even against a second Ruby run. Go's runtime also renders the same errno differently ('open /p: no such file or directory' against 'No such file or directory - A directory component in /p... does not exist'). ONLY that innermost detail is masked: the 'change from X to Y failed: ' prefix, the 'Could not set V on P: ' wrapper and the ' (file: F, line: N)' suffix all stay compared, because the property, the transition, the value being set and the manifest line are the attribution this gate exists to check. Applied where an event's status is 'failure' and where a log's level is 'err' -- the same selector, since event.rb:164 logs a failure at :err and everything else at :notice -- because a failed change is recorded as both an event and a log, and eliding one alone would leave the unreproducible text compared in the other
normalisation.failure_detail (validate_cmd exec failur: the one allowlist candidate the validate_cmd measurement names (file-validate-cmd.md section 3 item 6, D-48 (a)): a validator that cannot be executed fails with 'Execution of <cmd> returned 1: ' on both sides, but Ruby's text after it is whatever the forked child's log destinations wrote into the pipe -- measured as an ANSI-coloured 'Error: Could not execute posix command: No such file or directory - <argv0>' on the console and as a Ruby EBADF backtrace with --logdest <file> -- so it depends on how the agent was started and is not reproducible. failure_detail's ExecutionFailure branch already masks exactly that tail and nothing else, so no further entry is needed; the prefix, argv and status stay compared
normalisation.validate_cmd_temp_name: a failing validate_cmd's message embeds the substituted temp path, '<base><YYYYMMDD>-<pid>-<base36 rand>' (file_system/uniquefile.rb:102-116, measured as e.g. 'f20261007-41-jo66lh'), whose date, pid and random token differ between two RUBY runs. maskValidateTempNames masks only those three parts, and only inside the command of an 'Execution of ... returned' wrapper, under the failure_detail selectors; the directory, the base name and the naming shape stay compared, so a temp file named any other way diverges
